---
title: "Change Log"
---

## Summary so far

As of 2026-09, the copied BCFMS/MS codebase has been replaced by a PPSV
repository delivery. The new app is branded for PPSV, starts from a fresh
database, uses the PPSV service modules and inquiry flow, stores requests with
the shared `PPSV000001` sequence, records the required status/history/mail/file
metadata, and excludes the old MS cost, invoice, sample-table, and data-release
workflows.

The repository now contains the Shiny app, database migrations, tests,
deployment and provisioning scripts, Apache/Shiny templates, backup and restore
helpers, example non-secret configuration, and this operator guide. The code was
verified locally with R parsing, testthat tests, shell syntax checks, Quarto
rendering, and a browser smoke test.

Production activation is still gated on four administrator-owned items: the
matching TLS private key, authorization of `ppsv-service@biochem.mpg.de`, a real
ticket auto-reply/requester test, and an off-host recovery/pool snapshot policy.

## Latest repository changes

### 2026-10-19

- Added Ubuntu's `libuv1-dev` build dependency required by the locked `fs`
  package, and enabled `renv` package-cache symlinks so completed package
  installs are reused across releases without copying full libraries.
- Aligned maintenance-lock validation with provisioning: lock files may be
  owned by the runtime user inside the root-owned, non-writable lock directory.
- Directed `renv`'s user-level download/index cache into private persistent
  storage and set a valid runtime `HOME`, so R startup does not resolve a
  missing `/home/ppsvf-shiny-user` directory.
- Updated provisioning for the existing NSS-managed Shiny account: it keeps
  `/home/ppsvf-shiny-user` as the account's home, creates that private home and
  installs its `.Renviron`, and no longer tries to create or modify a duplicate
  local account. This handles Shiny Server's login-style `su` launch, which
  resets `HOME` and otherwise prevented `renv` from creating its cache.
- Made the root-run deployment cleanliness check read-only for Git's index, so
  it cannot replace the operator checkout's `.git/index` with a root-owned one.
- Stopped provisioning from changing the NFS pool root's ownership, mode, or
  ACL. Provisioning and deployment now verify actual service-user directory
  creation/removal; application storage no longer relies on `test -w` or
  `file.access()` for the pool.
- Kept `2770`/`0660` checks on PPSV-created project paths, while leaving
  facility pool-root permissions to the separate operator workflow.

### 2026-10-18

- Updated the Ubuntu 26.04 FreeType preflight to check the installed
  `libfreetype-dev` package name, avoiding a repeated no-op install.
- Pinned PPSV provisioning, deployment, Shiny Server, and maintenance workers
  to side-by-side R 4.6.1 at `/opt/R/4.6.1/bin`; the VM-wide `/usr/bin/R` remains
  unchanged.
- Changed persistent data to `/srv/ppsv-app-data`: pool-outage uploads remain in
  `uploads_pending_pool/`, while weekly verified local copies go to
  `db-backups/`. Local copies are not off-host disaster recovery.
- Added a five-minute health monitor with change-only operator email to
  `omicsdesk@biochem.mpg.de` for pool/fallback, missing project files,
  database, backup, mail-outbox, low disk space, Apache, and Shiny failures.
  Alert delivery depends on the SMTP relay.
- Configured the example for anonymous SMTP via `msx.biochem.mpg.de:25`.

- Kept `ppsvf-shiny-user` in `b_profa` for project-pool access while moving
  SQLite into an app-only `0700` directory with `0600` database files.
- Restricted database backups, maintenance locks, and the R dependency cache
  so other `b_profa` members cannot use them to bypass application controls.
- Updated provisioning, deployment, restore, verification, and tests for the
  private database path and permissions.

### 09-26-2026

- change the app name from ppsv-app to ppsvf-aap
- change group membership of ppsvf-shiny-user to the PPSVF group.
- add github synchronisation instructions
- clone repo to github

### 09-25-2026

- Added PPSV-specific Shiny modules, database schema, validation, PDF export,
  mail outbox, file storage, authorization, and admin views.
- Added idempotent provisioning, deployment, rollback, verification, backup,
  restore, pool reconciliation, and mail-processing scripts.
- Added PPSV operator documentation covering setup, fields, LDAP, SMTP,
  storage, TLS, backup/restore, acceptance, troubleshooting, and local

- Removed the copied MS runtime assumptions from the delivered application:
  production uses a fresh PPSV database and does not migrate `ms_projects.db`.
